text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your high blood pressure, can you tell me your age and if you have noticed any headaches, vision changes, or nosebleeds?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Since he is asymptomatic and this is a well-child visit, could you please tell me what his current blood pressure readings are? Also, have you noticed any abdominal masses or changes in his urinary habits, such as frequency or color?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
High blood pressure in a 5-year-old is significant, especially if isolated to one arm. I need to assess for coarctation of the aorta or renal artery stenosis. Let me check his pulses and blood pressure in all four extremities to look for discrepancies.

REQUEST TEST: BP_all_extremities
REQUEST TEST: Renal_Ultrasound

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: BP_all_extremities: Upper extremity blood pressure is 150/80 mm Hg in the right upper extremity and significantly higher than lower extremity blood pressure. Pulses are 2+ in radial arteries but trace in femoral arteries, indicating a pulse delay/discrepancy. Renal_Ultrasound: Normal renal anatomy with no evidence of renal artery stenosis or renal parenchymal disease. Echocardiogram findings confirm coarctation of the aorta with narrowing distal to the left subclavian artery and a pressure gradient.
